version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: Correctness release: our BS.1770-4 RLB filter was non-conformant, and every loudness figure Inseglet has ever reported read LOW by a constant. Surface UNCHANGED (190 tools / 3 resources / 5 prompts) - no new verbs, no new parameters. *** THIS BREAKS NUMERIC COMPARABILITY WITH v1.9.0 AND EARLIER for ABSOLUTE loudness. *** Figures reported by any prior release are low by 0.047099 / 0.043277 / 0.023566 / 0.021652 LU at 44.1 / 48 / 88.2 / 96 kHz. RELATIVE quantities - channel balances, deltas, ratios, LRA, activity fractions - are unaffected, because the correction is a pure gain at every frequency and the shift cancels. Add the constant for your sample rate to compare archived absolute figures against v1.10.0 output. The K-weighting stage-2 (RLB) highpass divided its numerator by a0, forcing the passband gain to exactly 1.000000000000. BS.1770-4 Table 1 keeps that numerator as exactly [1, -2, 1] - it is not normalised - and its gain is a0 = 1.004994898715 at 48 kHz. The -0.691 calibration term is defined against the TABULATED filter, so the normalised form read low by the constant above at every frequency. Moved by the fix: analysis.meter's channelsDetail[].kLevelLkfs, accessor_meter, object_loudness, stem_loudness, dialog_loudness, downmix_loudness, gatedLoudness() and the intent sidecar's expectLufs claims. The K-weighting shelf gain constant was also truncated to 12 significant digits where the reference carries 16, reaching b1 as a 1.044942e-12 error against Table 1. Worth about 3.3e-12 LU - below every measurement - but it was the whole of a discrepancy that had been attributed to the table's own precision rather than to us. Verified live against a running REAPER on 28 windows: the shift reproduced to 3.5e-12 LU and the cross-engine residual column came back invariant to 3.5e-12 LU. Cross-checked against a second independent BS.1770-4 implementation on 13 rows: the two now agree to 1.7799e-12 LU, where before the fix they differed by exactly the constant above - with Inseglet on the low side and the other implementation conformant. unit.meter now gates all five coefficients of BOTH filter stages against Table 1 at 1e-12, with a negative control that rejects the pre-fix numerator. The previous check gated the K-curve against flatness at 1 kHz to +/- 1.2 dB, which is 28x too loose to see a 0.043 dB error.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: Correctness release: 7.1.2 bed loudness, the identity-tone cache, and a routing detector that had been reporting false faults on 22.2. Surface UNCHANGED (190 tools / 3 resources / 5 prompts) - this release adds one parameter and no verbs. analysis.verify_routing gave FALSE VERDICTS on 22.2. 22.2 is the only bed layout declaring two LFE slots, and the plan put the one 40 Hz LFE tone on both, so the tone set was not unique. A PERFECTLY ROUTED 24-channel render came back ok=false, with channel 3 "bleed" at a margin of exactly 0.000000000 dB and channel 9 "duplicated", both at planCoverage 1.000000 - nothing in the numbers signalled it. Reaching it required doing exactly what the tool's own description instructs (passing back the echoed lfeChannels); with them omitted the same width read a clean 24/24, which is why it went unseen. The detector now REFUSES a degenerate plan outright and returns NO per-channel verdicts, rather than attaching a warning to a wrong answer. 7.1.2 beds received NO BS.1770-4 channel weights, reading 0.350 LU LOW. bedChannelLabels() enumerated cases 1/2/6/8/12/16 with no case 10, while the LFE predicate beside it generalised - so a layout the product accepts silently lost its weights while reporting "multichannel". 7.1.2 is the default bedLayout in three spatial tool schemas, and the bed.expectLufs claim consumed by iamf-sentinel-pro's intent-compare inherited the error. spatial.inject_identity_tones advertised "7.1.2" in its own schema enum and then refused it at runtime. Every bed-layout width now derives from ONE canonical table; five hand-rolled per-consumer width mappings are deleted. A registry-walking guard asserts that every layout any tool advertises is accepted at runtime, so a tool written later is covered by default. spatial.inject_identity_tones served STALE AUDIO after a parameter change. Files were named by slot index alone, so two calls with different parameters shared one path; REAPER installs a per-path PCM cache on the second access, and from then on a rewrite of that path is invisible - the tool reported the parameters it was asked for while REAPER played the earlier audio. Filenames now carry a hash of the WAV bytes, so identical parameters still give identical paths (determinism holds, and the cache hit is then correct) while different parameters can no longer collide at all. NEW: spatial.inject_identity_tones gains constantHz - one frequency on every slot, LFE included, so a multichannel fixture can hold a single frequency. The 313 + 139k plan cannot express that. A plan carrying it is a level instrument, not a routing one, and the routing detector refuses it by construction.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: IAMF ingest + in-DAW QC (190 tools / 3 resources / 5 prompts; was 187 / 3 / 4). spatial.export_adm now emits every audioObject before any audioChannelFormat, fixing a whole-file rejection by iamf-tools' ADM importer ("Failed to parse gain") — v1.7.0 exports were refused outright. No emitted byte changed, only the order the three groups are joined. New dolbyMetadataChunk:"placeholder" (default "none", and INDEPENDENT of profile) emits a placeholder `dbmd` chunk AND renames the bed to Dolby's RoomCentric* vocabulary — one switch, because a consumer only reads those names when a `dbmd` is present — so the importer keeps the objects instead of failing the encode with "No audioObject present". It fails closed, with the remedy named, on non-24-bit, a rate outside {48k, 96k}, or a bed outside 5.1 / 7.1 / 7.1.2, and a runtime advisory discloses the trade on four surfaces. New author_dolby_adm prompt (5th). spatial.inject_identity_tones + analysis.verify_routing: in-DAW channel-identity QC. A unique tone per bed channel or object track (313 + 139k Hz, LFE 40 Hz, -18 dBFS) read back from a rendered WAV or a render-free track accessor, reporting identity / swapped / duplicated / dropped / bleed / silent per channel with a measured margin — catches the routing fault class inside the session, before export, and independently verifies Inseglet's own send encodings. envelope.ensure_fx_envelope: ensures an FX-parameter envelope exists and returns the name envelope.add_point looks up (add_point could only write to an already-active envelope, and autoActivate reaches only REAPER's built-in track envelopes). Tiered parameter resolution that refuses an ambiguous request by naming its candidates instead of silently picking one.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: B1 intent sidecar (authoring side) + representation-aware positioning. No surface-count change (187 tools / 3 resources / 4 prompts). intentSidecar: true on spatial.export_adm and spatial.export_loom_manifest writes the session's own predictions beside the export (<base>.intent.json / manifest.intent.json, schema intent: 0): per-channel bed level claims (BS.1770-4-conformant whole-bed weights), object trajectories at block reach times, SN3D projection-decode dominance/coverage predictions, per-ACN scene RMS. Never a declared deliverable loudness — every level is an expect* claim for the open iamf-sentinel-pro consumer (sentinel intent-compare, S-340..S-346). Silent-channel claims floor at the BS.1770 silence convention (-70 LKFS), verified through a live REAPER -> export -> consumer gate. spatial.set_source_position now drives azimuth/elevation on angle-representation panners (IEM/SPARTA-style encoders) instead of bare-letter param matching, which could land on Quaternion X — or read "aZimuth" as z — and move params the ADM exporter never samples; ReaSurroundPan-style cartesian writes are unchanged, and auto-detect finds angle panners without an explicit fx index.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: IAMF delivery: the Loom bridge + cross-ecosystem docs (187 tools / 3 resources / 4 prompts; includes the 1.5.1 correctness patch). spatial.export_loom_manifest: one call renders the session's bed (stereo/5.1/7.1.4) and/or ambisonic scene (order 1-4, ACN/SN3D) plus per-language VO stems as 48 kHz integer-PCM WAVs in iamf-loom's channel order and emits the loom: 0 manifest (+ optional season.yaml); `loom compile` accepts the output as-is and every packaged deliverable is gated by the iamf-sentinel validator. Channel mapping is identity (spelling-only label deltas), verified with per-channel identity tones. Never writes a loudness value (Loom measures); objects fail closed to the ADM route (spatial.export_adm). New deliver_to_iamf expert prompt (4th) walks inventory -> per-mix channel-budget check (the M-416 class) -> dryRun preview -> export -> loom compile/run. New MANUAL section 9 "Delivering to IAMF" documents the pipeline end to end.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: Correctness-first patch release; no surface change (186 tools). BS.1770-4 bed channel weights now read Tables 4/5 exactly (boundary-inclusive: 1.41 only at ear level within |az| 60-120): rear surrounds Lsr/Rsr (M+/-135) 1.41 -> 1.00; wides Lw/Rw (M+/-060, 9.1.6) 1.00 -> 1.41. Every loudness tool inherits; 7.1-family readings move <= ~1.5 dB of affected-channel contribution; 5.1/stereo/22.2 unchanged. ADM hardening: writer azimuth wrap + elevation clamp + distance floor at spherical serialization; LFE <frequency> at its BS.2076 home (audioChannelFormat); real ds64.riffSize on BW64. adm_profile_check now classifies common-definitions ADM (previously invisible: HOA/binaural/multi-programme/oversize beds correctly non-conformant), gates bed layouts against the BS.2094 table, enforces single-programme + 24-bit, and verifies the interpolationLength ramp (new code: interpolation_ramp). adm_inspect gains a per-channel summary + packTypes census and a corrected version readout.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: First public macOS release. In-process MCP server (Streamable HTTP + SSE, JSON-RPC 2.0, MCP 2025-06-18); loopback-only transport with a bearer token; every mutation single-undo. 186 tools / 3 resources / 3 prompts, with immersive/spatial audio as the differentiator: channel beds (5.1–22.2), ambisonic encode/decode + order/format conversion (ACN/SN3D), surround panners, binaural monitoring + live head-tracking; native ADM BWF and Dolby Atmos Master File (.atmos triad) authoring + inspection; bed/object send-layout orchestration for an external renderer; immersive metering (ITU-R BS.1770 loudness, DirAC/Gerzon spatial field, per-object loudness, decode-coverage + per-object decode-coverage timelines); deliverable-spec conformance; immersive style chains with a multichannel true-peak limiter; a composite macro DSL; and async MCP elicitation for destructive confirmation.

metadata.description: A native REAPER extension exposing a first-class Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface, with immersive / spatial audio as the primary differentiator. Loopback-only transport with a bearer token; every mutation is single-undo. macOS-first; Windows/Linux to follow once load-verified.
